detailZh: F1西班牙大奖赛值得关注的五件事
本周末西班牙大奖赛将迎来新的举办地
本周末，一级方程式将迎来西班牙大奖赛的新主办地，马德里环赛道将在西班牙首都郊区首次亮相。
它将取代此前举办西班牙大奖赛的巴塞罗那，后者仍在F1赛历上，但已更名为新名称，并已于6月举办了其2026年的比赛——由刘易斯·汉密尔顿夺冠。
本周末将是马德里自1981年老牌哈拉马赛道以来首次出现在F1赛历上，这也是大奖赛期间众多热议话题之一。
以下是值得关注的五件事。
任何新赛事都需要一定的磨合期。以第一届迈阿密大奖赛为例，餐饮设施位置欠佳，导致难以为贵宾区提供热食。
哦不！难道没有人会心疼那些可怜的VIP和他们变冷的开胃小点吗？
要知道，蒙扎举办大奖赛的历史远早于世界锦标赛的创办，而进出赛道至今仍是一场纯粹混乱的考验。阿布扎比也是如此，自2009年起每年举办F1，访客们却常常纳闷，为何大门口的安排依然一团糟。
因此，当我们的赛道团队抵达马德里赛道时（好吧，也许Fil除外，他仍被困在巴塞罗那与马德里之间的某趟火车上），找不到任何从媒体中心到围场的路，也就不足为奇了。同样被发现四处游荡、一脸茫然（两头茫然）的还有Pedro de la Rosa和安东内利。
后勤混乱将加剧车队搭建设备时面临的挑战，尤其这是背靠背赛事的第二站。假设车手们能找到他们的车库，而且那里有车可开，谁又能预料一旦赛车上道会出现什么样的乱子呢？
新铺设的沥青往往会出现问题，不过据说路面已经过高压清洗以去除油性残留物。而且，在一大堆线路最近被盗之后，我们只能希望所有的标识牌还能正常运作……
上周末的意大利大奖赛，或许是乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔）首次公开承认他的总冠军希望实际上已经破灭。这位梅赛德斯车手在蒙扎获得亚军，负于队友基米·安东内利（安东内利），这意味着这位20岁的意大利车手目前在剩下10轮比赛的情况下已建立起66分的领先优势。
“是啊，基米确实掌控着局面，而且他有资格掌控局面，”他说。“我甚至都没有去想什么争夺或者反击之类的事情。我只是专注于一场一场比赛地对待，努力在每个周末都做到最好。”
“他的表现极其出色。要弥补这个差距将非常困难，所以我基本上就是接受现实吧。从现在开始我只想享受比赛，并尽可能多地赢下比赛。”
这肯定不是拉塞尔所预想的2026年赛季走向。赛季开始时，他是众望所归的夺冠大热门，并在墨尔本揭幕战中从杆位发车并夺冠，印证了这一标签。然而随后几轮比赛中运气并没有站在他这边，比如日本的时机不巧的安全车。但蒙扎一役恰恰证明了安东内利为什么是当之无愧的领跑者——要知道，他可是从第19位发车的！
如果拉塞尔（Russell）在那样一个周末都无法占据优势——那个周末他二年级队友还带着罚退发车——那么很难看出他还能在哪里占据上风并实现翻盘。
所以本周末的马德里大奖赛只是安东内利（Antonelli）加冕之路上又一场比赛——而且不要赌他在2026年拿不到第八场胜利！
角田裕毅（Tsunoda）本为一次性回归，如今已变成三场比赛
不久之前，多家F1媒体——包括本媒体在内——还把角田裕毅在赞德沃特的回归称为“一次性出场”。然而，现在这位日本车手即将为小红牛车队进行他今年第三次大奖赛正赛发车，同样地，劳森（劳森）也将继续为红牛车队出战。
这是由于红牛常规车手伊萨克·哈贾尔（哈贾尔）仍在与八月夏休期间在健身房训练中受伤的手腕伤势作斗争，他先缺席了赞德福特站，随后又缺席了蒙扎站，而马德里站将使他连续缺席第三场比赛。
虽然这对哈贾尔来说显然令人失望，但对于劳森和角田裕毅来说，这却是一个绝佳的机会，因为两人2026年的计划都尚未确定。对劳森而言，他或许应该对自己的未来最为放松，因为这位新西兰车手今年在小红牛的表现确实令人印象深刻，稳定地获得积分，并在过去两轮为红牛出战时表现英勇。
与此同时，角田裕毅尚未获得2026年的全职席位，据了解他正在洽谈明年参加IndyCar的比赛。因此他不太可能获得2027年的F1席位，但他并没有放弃全部希望，马德里站只是他展示自己真正实力的又一次机会——去年在红牛的艰难经历损害了他大部分声誉。
这位日本车手在赞德福特表现稳健，随后在蒙扎拿到了一个积分，考虑到小红牛目前领跑中游集团，如果他再取得一个前十名的成绩，也不必过于惊讶。
上个月当F3前往马德里赛道进行官方测试时，一些车队老板和赞助商可能会感到困惑。最终结果是出现了19次红旗，其中包括多起重大撞车事故，推高了事故账单。
与任何新赛道一样，第一年的抓地力水平会极低。但马德里赛道由公共道路和缓冲区极少的定制高速路段混合而成，很可能导致一个混乱的周末。
很多注意力将集中在马德里赛道的标志性特点——坡度陡峭的La Monumental弯道上，它比乍看起来要复杂得多，具有变化的半径和海拔变化。
但在令人印象深刻的12号弯之前和之后的弯角也极其棘手，有很多出弯墙直接延伸回赛道而不是逐渐远离。由于有如此多的未知因素，这项赛事的首届比赛很有可能变得一团糟。
"我认为，考虑到他们设置的护栏和赛道的设计，这肯定会是近来一级方程式最大的挑战之一，"担任该赛事大使的塞恩斯说。
"这条赛道让我想起很多吉达，让我想起很多巴库，在某些方面甚至让我有点想起澳门。所以开着1000马力的F1赛车跑这样的赛道，将会是一个非常有趣的挑战。"
Sainz知道F3测试中发生的事情，他并不抱有幻想：马德里赛道可能会成为混乱的温床，无论是在排位赛中车手们在距离护墙仅几毫米处寻找极限，还是随时可能出现的阻挡事故的威胁。
"我一直在研究这条赛道，也听说了F3测试中发生的事情，"他补充道。"我想我们都在预期排位赛中会出现安全车、红旗和黄旗之类的情况。"
“最近一级方程式有前往这类赛道的趋势，比如吉达和巴库，它们更靠近市区，还有迈阿密，但这些赛道有更多的护墙，而我们没有遇到过任何问题。”,
在汉密尔顿发表“没有规则”的言论后，法拉利成为了焦点
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
继两位法拉利车手在蒙扎发生碰撞之后，本周末所有人的目光都将聚焦于在马德里的汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔，以及车队是否会回应这位英国车手对更明确车队规则的呼吁。
勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿在周日发车时并排驶入一号弯的减速弯。这位七届世界冠军在1号弯选择了内线，但这位摩纳哥车手守住位置并在2号弯抢到内侧线路，没有给他的队友留下任何空间，队友被迫驶入砂石区，因此损失了多个名次，引发了愤怒。
汉密尔顿认为自己本应获得优先权，因为他在车手积分榜上比勒克莱尔更接近梅赛德斯两位车手，他还借此抨击法拉利，回忆起自己在梅赛德斯时期事情的运作方式，声称马拉内罗“没有任何规则”。
当F1前往陌生的马德里赛道赛道时，法拉利对该赛道已有一定了解，因为车队曾在7月在那里进行过一次拍摄日。这是否会带来优势还有待观察，但可以肯定的是：法拉利必须让两位车手之间达成更清晰的理解，才能前往西班牙大奖赛。
detailEn: Five things to look out for at the F1 Spanish GP
There will be a new host of the Spanish Grand Prix this weekend
Formula 1 will welcome a new host of the Spanish Grand Prix this weekend as the Madring will make its debut on the outskirts of Spain’s capital city.
It is replacing previous Spanish GP holder Barcelona, which is still on the F1 calendar but under a new name having hosted its 2026 race in June - won by Lewis Hamilton.
This weekend will be the first time Madrid has appeared on the F1 calendar since the old-school Jarama circuit in 1981 and is one of many things that will be a talking point during the grand prix.
So here are five things to look out for.

With any new event there’s a certain amount of bedding in. Take the first iteration of the Miami Grand Prix, where the sub-optimal location of the catering facilities led to difficulties supplying hot food to the hospitality enclosures.
Oh no! Will nobody think of the poor VIPs and their cold canapes?

Mind you, Monza has been hosting grands prix since long before the world championship began and simply getting in and out of the track remains an essay in pure chaos. Ditto Abu Dhabi, where visitors often have cause to ponder why the arrangements at the gate remain a fustercluck when they’ve been hosting F1 annually since 2009.

To that end it was no surprise when our track team arrived at the Madring (well, maybe not Fil, still trapped on a train somewhere between Barcelona and Madrid) and couldn’t find any way to get from the media centre to the paddock. Also spotted wandering around looking lost: Pedro de la Rosa and Kimi Antonelli.

Logistical disarray will add to the challenges facing the teams setting up their equipment, given that this is the second race of a double-header. Assuming the drivers can find their way to their garages, and that there are cars there to drive, who knows what manner of malarkey could ensue once the cars hit the track?

Recently laid asphalt has a habit of misbehaving, although apparently the surface has been pressure-washed to get rid of the oily residues. And let’s hope all the signage still works, after a whole bunch of wiring was stolen recently…

Last weekend’s Italian Grand Prix was perhaps the first time George Russell publicly acknowledged that his title hopes were practically over. The Mercedes driver finished runner-up to team-mate Kimi Antonelli at Monza, meaning the 20-year-old Italian has now established a 66-point lead with 10 rounds remaining.

"Yeah, Kimi's definitely in control of it and he's deserving to be in control of it," he said. "I'm not even thinking about a fight or a comeback or anything. I'm just focused on taking it race by race and trying to maximise every single weekend.

"He's performing incredibly well. It's going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap, so I'm just sort of accepting that is what it is. I'm just going to enjoy it from here on in and try and win as many races as possible."

This is certainly not how Russell thought 2026 would pan out, entering the season as the heavy title favourite and supporting that tag by winning the Melbourne opener from pole. Luck subsequently didn’t go his way in the following rounds, such as the untimely safety car in Japan, but Monza was demonstrative of how Antonelli is the deserving leader – considering he started the race in 19th!
If Russell can’t even take advantage on a weekend like that, where his sophomore team-mate was carrying a grid penalty, then it’s hard to see where he will hold the upper hand and perform a comeback.
So Madrid this weekend is just another race on the path to Antonelli’s crowning moment – and don’t bet against him taking an eighth victory of 2026!
The one-off Tsunoda return that has turned into three races

It wasn’t long ago that several F1 media outlets – this one included – were labelling Yuki Tsunoda’s return at Zandvoort as a ‘one-off appearance’. Yet, here we are, with the Japanese driver set to make his third grand prix start of the year for Racing Bulls, likewise for Liam Lawson at Red Bull.

This comes as the result of usual Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar still battling with a wrist injury that he sustained during a gym session over the August summer break, first missing Zandvoort and then Monza, with Madrid set to make it three in a row.

While it obviously comes as a disappointment for Hadjar, it has presented a golden opportunity for both Lawson and Tsunoda with neither of their plans for 2026 yet confirmed. For Lawson, he should probably be the most relaxed over his future as the Kiwi has certainly impressed for Racing Bulls this year by scoring consistent points finishes and performing valiantly in the past two rounds for Red Bull.

Tsunoda, meanwhile, has been without a full-time seat in 2026 and is understood to be in talks for an IndyCar drive next year. So a spot on the F1 grid in 2027 is unlikely, but he hasn’t given up all hope and Madrid is just another chance for him to show what he can actually do after his torrid Red Bull stint last year damaged much of his reputation.

The Japanese driver performed solidly in Zandvoort before scoring a point in Monza, and considering Racing Bulls is leading the midfield, one shouldn’t be too shocked if he were to claim another top 10 result.

When F3 headed to the Madring for an official test last month, some team owners and sponsors will have likely scratched their heads. The end result was 19 red flags, including a number of significant crashes that drove up the accident bills.

As is always the case with any new circuit, the grip levels will be extremely low in year one. But Madring's hybrid of public roads and bespoke high-speed sections with little runoff area could well lead to a chaotic weekend.
A lot of attention will go to the Madring's headline feature, the steeply banked La Monumental curve and is a lot more complex than it first seems, with its varying radii and elevation changes.

But the corners right before and after the impressive Turn 12 are also extremely tricky, with plenty of exit walls that come back into the track rather than fade away. With so many unknowns, there is every chance the first running of the event could become a messy one.

"I think definitely with the way they've put the barriers and the design of the track, it's going to be one of the biggest challenges in Formula 1 recently," said Carlos Sainz, who is an ambassador for the event.

"The track reminds me a lot of Jeddah, reminds me a lot of Baku, even reminds me a bit of Macau in some ways. So having that in an F1 car with 1,000 horsepower is going to be quite an interesting challenge."

Sainz was aware of what happened in the F3 test and was under no illusion that the Madring could be a recipe for chaos, both in qualifying with drivers searching for the limit millimetres away from the walls, and the omnipresent threat of impeding incidents.
"I've been looking at the track and hearing of what happened in the F3 test,” he added. “I think we are all expecting safety cars and red flags and yellow flags in qualifying and things like this.
“It's been a tendency of Formula 1 to go to these kinds of tracks like Jeddah and Baku recently, that are closer to the city, Miami, but they have more walls and we haven't had any issues with it."
Ferrari is under the spotlight after Hamilton’s “there are no rules” remarks
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

Eyes will be on Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Madrid this weekend following the clash between the two Ferrari drivers at Monza, and on whether the team will respond to the Briton’s calls for clearer team rules.

Leclerc and Hamilton went side by side into the opening chicane at the start on Sunday. The seven-time world champion went for the inside at Turn 1, but the Monegasque held on and took the inside line for Turn 2, leaving no room for his team-mate, who was forced into the gravel and consequently lost several positions, causing anger.

Hamilton felt he should have been given priority, as he is closer to the Mercedes duo than Leclerc in the drivers’ championship, and took a swipe at Ferrari by recalling how things worked during his time at Mercedes, claiming that “there are no rules” at Maranello.

While F1 heads into unknown territory at the Madring, Ferrari already has some knowledge of the venue from a filming day the team conducted there in July. Whether that will give it an advantage remains to be seen, but one thing is certain: Ferrari must arrive at the Spanish Grand Prix with a clearer understanding between its two drivers.

items.titleZh: 雅克·维伦纽夫谈从父亲吉尔身上真正学到的东西
items.summaryZh: 1997年世界冠军雅克·维伦纽夫表示，他从未把自己视为父亲吉尔·维伦纽夫赛车遗产的传承者，但如今承认自己从父亲身上吸收了更深层的东西——“我能做到，你做不到”。
items.originalTitle: 雅克·维伦纽夫从吉尔·维伦纽夫身上真正学到的东西：“我能做到，你做不到”
items.summaryEn: 1997 world champion Jacques Villeneuve says he never saw himself as carrying on his father Gilles' legacy in motor racing, but now recognises he absorbed something deeper from him: "I can do this, you can't".
detailZh: 雅克·维伦纽夫真正从吉尔身上学到的东西：“我能做到，你做不到”
这位1997年的世界冠军从未把自己视为父亲赛车遗产的继承者，但他现在表示，他意识到自己从吉尔身上吸收了某种更深层次的东西。
当明星英年早逝时，他们不可避免地会以永恒年轻的形象被困在大众的意识中，成为英勇高贵与牺牲精神这种浪漫化概念的化身。
对于赛车迷来说，吉尔·维伦纽夫那辉煌而激进的驾驶风格代表了车手应有的终极典范。他32岁时在佐尔德赛道1982年比利时大奖赛排位赛中丧生，使这位悲剧陨落英雄的神话更加根深蒂固。事故背后与队友迪迪埃·皮罗尼之间积怨的背景，至今仍是一个充满争议的话题。
当然，传奇背后这个人的真实面貌要复杂得多，这也解释了为什么他的儿子雅克在1996年进入一级方程式（Formula 1）时如此抗拒人们把他和父亲相提并论。
一部讲述他父亲不为人知的故事的传记电影《维伦纽夫：传奇的崛起》将于9月19日在多伦多国际电影节举行全球首映，随后将于11月在魁北克院线上映。全球上映定于明年，届时正好是吉尔勒于1977年英国大奖赛驾驶迈凯伦完成一级方程式首秀50周年。
影片将聚焦于吉尔勒成为法拉利偶像之前的岁月，那是一段充满个人和职业挫折的曲折旅程。雅克的妹妹梅拉妮是执行制片人。
1978年意大利大奖赛上，吉尔勒·维伦纽夫与妻子乔安娜以及子女梅拉妮和雅克的合影
"谈论我爸爸从来都不是问题," 雅克告诉Motorsport.com。"问题在于那些人（记者）对我的回答不感兴趣，也不关心我的想法。"
"他们根本不在乎。他们只想听到的是，'我是在延续我爸爸未竟的事业，这就是我参赛的原因'。不，我赛车是因为我热爱赛车。就这么简单。"
"我爱我的爸爸。我为他感到骄傲——他很了不起，他取得的成就令人敬佩。但我在走自己的路。我赛车不是为了成为吉尔·维伦纽夫的延续。这没什么问题。"
"而他们因此生气了。所以那时我说，'好吧，我再也不想谈论他了，因为这毫无意义。这根本不是一场有建设性的讨论。你们其实根本不在乎。'"
本周，一级方程式（Formula 1）自1981年以来首次造访马德里。当年在哈拉马（Jarama）举办的最后一届西班牙大奖赛上，吉尔·维伦纽夫（Gilles Villeneuve）赢得了他职业生涯的最后一场胜利——驾驶一辆操控极差的法拉利，上演了一堂教科书式的防守驾驶课。
吉尔·维伦纽夫（Gilles Villeneuve）最令人难忘的特质之一就是永不放弃——就像1979年在赞德沃特（Zandvoort）那样，他尝试骑着三个轮子把赛车开回维修区。
父亲去世时，雅克（Jacques）刚满11岁，之后他的许多成长岁月都在寄宿学校度过。由于吉尔（Gilles）痴迷地专注于自己的赛车生涯，他父母的婚姻一直承受着压力。
雅克（Jacques）说：“他去世的时候，我真的已经一两年没见过他了。他其实并没有和我们住在一起，那真的是一种很奇怪的状况。”
"所以我从来不知道那是一段真实的记忆，还是我成长过程中被灌输的记忆，主要是我母亲当年讲的。这让人非常困惑。"
"所以现在，能够在成长历程上填补一些空白的感觉很好。我认为这部影片对那些成长岁月的刻画是相当准确的。"
维伦纽夫是仅有的三位身为辉煌F1车手之子的世界冠军之一。实际上，这三位进入赛车运动的原因各不相同，并且与父亲留下的遗产有着复杂的关系。
雅克现在为F1电视频道（F1 TV）和Canal+电视台担任解说嘉宾。
例如，雅克的前队友达蒙·希尔就曾做过一段摩托车快递员，因为他父亲格雷厄姆在空难中丧生后的诉讼使家庭陷入了财务困境。尼科·罗斯伯格的父亲科科是1982年的世界冠军，他在尼科的卡丁车生涯中只保持一定距离的参与，之后一直保持低调。尼科本可以从事工程行业，但他拒绝了伦敦帝国理工学院的录取，选择专注赛车。
父母曾是成功车手的人，在尝试追求类似职业生涯时，往往会为期望的重负所困扰。
维伦纽夫说：“如果你是出于错误的原因从事这项运动，你永远无法成功。你必须发自内心地、真正地热爱它。要愿意承受打击，因为你会遭受很多打击。
“在计时成绩上你很容易被打回原形，就是这么简单。你会如何应对呢？”
"主要是在你的成长期，当你开始跑三级方程式的时候。那是你挨打最狠的阶段。所以你需要在自己周围建立起一层保护壳。
"事情之所以是那样，就是这个原因。但那之后反而给了我自由，让我可以只做自己，而不必背负什么。
"我觉得这一点我在不知不觉中从父亲身上学到了很多。不是因为他作为车手是什么样的人，而是因为他在不在赛车里的时候是什么样的人——而这完全是同一个人。他在家里和在赛道的赛车里一模一样。
"无论他在做什么，他总在想做的东西上非常自我。他确实爱他的家人等等，但他非常自我，因为他是唯一一个想在自己想开皮卡的时候开皮卡、想爬山的时候去爬山的人。而那才是唯一重要的事。
“而且只要我们陪他一起玩他那些玩意儿，他就可以和我们玩。就是这样。小时候能和他一起坐上他的皮卡，那时候我就好像置身天堂一样酷。
“但后来我能看到他对风险的态度，挑战极限，但带着尊重。尊重对手。而且总是渴望战胜下一个挑战。
“而且他经常这么做只是为了向其他人证明：‘我能做到，你做不到’。因为这基本上就是他的人生故事：‘我能做到，你做不到’。
“甚至他买了自己的直升机之后，还试图做翻筋斗飞行，就因为有人告诉他做不到。类似这种事情。
“在那个方面，我从他身上学到了很多。但教育方式不同。所以我觉得这让我在计算风险时能做得稍微好一点。
“但对于他作为父亲的样子，我没有太多记忆。我不知道是因为那些记忆本来就不存在，还是因为在他去世后我把它们封存了起来。那是我活下去的方式。
“令人惊叹的是，在过去几年里，人们纷纷敞开心扉，讲述他们和我父亲共事的时光。
“就连普罗斯特（Alain Prost），或者其他曾经和他同场竞技的人，我猜他们以前从未敢开口过。而我现在了解到的他，与我从母亲那里得到的形象是如此不同。”
多伦多国际电影节将于9月19日举办《维伦纽夫：传奇的崛起》的全球首映，该片将于11月在魁北克院线上映，随后于明年全球发行。
这是吉尔在1982年比利时大奖赛排位赛中遭遇致命事故前不久的最后几张影像之一。
detailEn: What Jacques Villeneuve really learned from Gilles: "I can do this, you can’t"
The 1997 world champion has never seen himself as carrying on his father’s legacy in motor racing, but he now says he recognises he absorbed something deeper from Gilles
When stars die young, they inevitably become trapped in the popular consciousness in a state of eternal youth, embodying romanticised notions of heroic nobility and sacrifice.

For motor racing fans, Gilles Villeneuve’s spectacular and aggressive style came to represent the epitome of what a racing driver should be. His death at the age of 32, during qualifying for the 1982 Belgian Grand Prix at Zolder, crystallised the myth of the tragically fallen hero. The background to the accident of rancour behind the scenes with team-mate Didier Pironi remains a controversial topic to this day.
The truth of the man behind the legend is rather more nuanced, of course, which accounts for why his son Jacques was so resistant to comparisons when he arrived in Formula 1 in 1996.

A new biopic telling the untold story of his father, Villeneuve: Rise of a Legend, will receive its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival on 19 September, ahead of a theatrical release in Quebec in November. Global release is scheduled for next year, 50 years after Gilles made his F1 debut in a McLaren at the 1977 British Grand Prix.
It will focus on the years before Gilles became a Ferrari icon, an eventful journey full of personal and professional setbacks. Jacques' sister Melanie is the executive producer.
Gilles Villeneuve with his wife, Joanna, and children Melanie and Jacques, at the 1978 Italian Grand Prix
"Talking about my dad was never an issue," Jacques told Motorsport.com. "The issue was those people [journalists] were not interested in my answer. Or my way of thinking.

"They could not care less. All they were wanting to hear is, ‘I'm carrying on the flame because of what my dad did not finish, and that's why I'm doing it’. No, I'm racing because I love racing. Simple.
"I loved my dad. I’m proud of him – he was amazing, what he achieved. But I'm doing my own thing. I’m not racing because I want to be the continuation of Gilles Villeneuve. That's okay.
"And they were getting angry. So that's when I said, ‘OK, I'm not even wanting to talk about him anymore because it's pointless. There's not a constructive discussion. You don't actually care.’"

This week Formula 1 visits Madrid for the first time since 1981, when the last Spanish Grand Prix to be held at Jarama was the scene of Gilles Villeneuve's final victory, a masterclass of defensive driving in an ill-handling Ferrari.
One of Gilles Villeneuve's abiding characteristics was his refusal to give up – as at Zandvoort in 1979, when he tried to drive back to the pits on three wheels
Jacques had just turned 11 when his father died and spent many of his formative years at a boarding school. His parents’ marriage was under strain as Gilles focused obsessively on his racing career.
"When he passed, I hadn't seen him for a year or two, really," said Jacques. "He wasn't really living with us. It was really an odd situation.
"So I never know if it's a real memory, or a memory I was told growing up, mainly by my mother at the time. So that's very confusing.
"So right now, it's nice to be able to put some dots on the thing. And I think that the movie is quite accurate on those formative years."

Villeneuve is one of just three world champions who were sons of glorious F1 drivers. All of them actually had different reasons for going into motor racing and conflicted relationships with their fathers’ legacies.
Jacques now works as a pundit for F1 TV and Canal+

Jacques' former team-mate Damon Hill, for instance, spent time working as a motorcycle courier because litigation after his father Graham’s death in a plane crash brought financial ruin on the family. Nico Rosberg’s father Keke, the 1982 world champion, had arm’s-length input in Nico’s karting career and maintained a low profile thereafter. Nico could have gone into engineering, but declined an offer from Imperial College London to focus on racing.
People whose parents were successful racers often struggle with the burden of expectations when they try to pursue a similar career.

"If you're doing this sport for the wrong reason, you'll never achieve it," said Villeneuve. "You have to really, personally, yourself, deep down, love it. Willing to take the punches because you get a lot of punches.
"You get put back in place very easily on the clock. It's very simple. How will you react to that?
"Mostly in your formative years, when you start in Formula 3. That's when you take the biggest beatings. So you need to build some kind of carapace around you.
"That's why it happened like that. But then that gave me the freedom to just be me and not really carry it.

"I think that's something I took a lot from my dad without knowing. Not because of who he was as a racer, but who he was when he was not in the race car – which was exactly the same guy. He was at home exactly the same way as he was at the racetrack in the race car.

"Whatever he was doing was always very selfish in what he was wanting to do. He did love his family and so on, but he was very selfish in the fact that he's the only one who wants to play on his pickup truck when he wants to climb a mountain. And that's all that mattered.
"And we could play with him if we did his things with him. That was it. As a boy that was super cool when I could go on his pickup truck with him at the same time, I was in paradise.
"But then I could see his attitude towards risk, pushing the limit, but with respect. With respect to the opposition. And just always wanting to beat the next challenge.
"And often doing it just showed the other guys, 'I can do it, you can't'. Because that was his life story basically: 'I can do this, you can't'.
"And even when he bought his chopper he was trying to do loop-the-loops because he’d been told it couldn’t do it. Stuff like that.
"I took a lot from him on that aspect. But with a different education. So I think it allowed me to calculate the risk just a little bit better.
"But I don't have a lot of memory of him as a father. I don't know if it's because they don't exist or because I've just put them away when he died. And that was my way of surviving.
"What's amazing is how over the last few years, people have opened up about their time with my dad.
"Even [Alain] Prost, or other people that used to race with him, that never dared before, I guess. And the picture I'm getting is so different than the one I got from my mother."

The Toronto International Film Festival will host the global premiere of Villeneuve: Rise of a Legend on 19 September, with a theatrical release in Quebec in November, ahead of a global release next year.

items.originalTitle: F1新马德里赛道为何被称为“赛车杀手”
items.summaryEn: This weekend's Madrid Grand Prix will debut the brand-new Madring circuit, which has been compared to a mix of Monaco, Macau and Jeddah, but fears about its "car killer" nature have arisen after 19 red flags and multiple damaged cars in an F3 test.
detailZh: 一级方程式的新西班牙大奖赛场地被形容为“赛车杀手”。
全新的马德里赛道赛道将于本周末举办史上第一场比赛，但直到现在F1车手们才开始意识到这条赛道将带来多么巨大的挑战。
已经驾驶过这条赛道的人将其描述为摩纳哥、澳门和吉达的混合体。
这是一条老派赛道，拥有真正的特色和有可能成为经典瞬间的弯角。但也有人担心它会带来什么样的比赛，以及对赛车和车手会有多么残酷。
在6月赛道建设期间探索过该赛道后，我们进一步深入研究了这条赛道究竟会带来什么样的挑战，以及本周末我们可以期待什么。
最大的指示是几周前在那里举行的为期两天的F3测试。
“在F3测试中出现了19次红旗和三个损坏的底盘、损坏的悬挂……好吧，他们是F3车手，但这是一条杀死赛车的赛道，”威廉姆斯F1车队领队James Vowles告诉西班牙媒体Sport。
The 比赛了解到，一些F3车队对不得不在那里测试感到不太满意，因为损坏零件清单非常长。
但那次F3测试作为F1马德里赛事的试播集非常有价值，这是赛道组织者要求的，试图避免拉斯维加斯首秀时出现的那些问题——当时失控的排水盖干扰了练习赛，撞毁了塞恩斯的法拉利，并激怒了车队领队Fred Vasseur。
混乱的F3测试也为F1车队和车手敲响了警钟，让他们意识到这将是一个多么大的挑战。
法拉利曾在7月在那里进行了一次F1拍摄日，但那时赛道版本要粗糙得多，所以F3的测试才是该场地的第一次正式测试。
让F1车队和车手担忧的是，F3中的19次红旗分散在赛道各处（见下文）。这意味着不仅仅有一个危险区域需要应对，而是有很多地方你可能出错并面临巨额维修账单。
由于许多车队要在2026年成本上限内计算剩余的开发预算，他们最不希望的就是赛车被撞毁。
我们采访了几位F3车手和车队，以了解为什么马德里赛道在这么多不同方面都如此具有挑战性，以及为什么会有这么多红旗。
当被问及为什么它如此具有挑战性时，奥迪支持的F3锦标赛领先者Freddie Slater告诉The 比赛：“因为那里的弯角非常紧，不容犯错，而且出弯时墙壁会向你逼近。它们不像大多数赛道那样远离你。”
“你总是出弯时试图远离它，而不是最大化利用，所以这是一条很难找到节奏的赛道。”
“你必须推进，否则你就慢。所以我认为这就是为什么它会造成这么多撞车，因为如果你不推进，你就没有达到极限。”
“但老实说，在我看来它可能是赛历上最好的赛道之一，因为它有那种老派的感觉。有点像一些老派的英国赛道、澳门之类的地方。所以我真的很兴奋能在那里举行[F3锦标赛]决赛。”
马德里赛道的一圈从类似吉达的低速减速弯开始，然后是3号和4号弯的全速冲刺，接着进入第一个真正的危险区域——第二个减速弯。
这是一个高速减速弯，出弯时墙壁肯定会向你逼近，也是测试中许多F3赛车被撞毁的地方。
“那里有很多圈速可赚，因为之后是上坡路段，所以上坡时有很多圈速可以争取，”Slater说。
“这就是为什么我看到很多人为了最大圈速而冒险，但这也可能是撞车最多的地方。”
“此外，路肩也不太宽容，所以你必须做对，否则就会撞车。”
这本质上是现已移除的新加坡Sling三顶点弯的更困难版本，轨迹是“如果稍微出错就会头朝墙壁撞去”。它不像虚拟世界中的一些圈那样看起来可以轻松跳过路肩。
而且减速弯的入口是赛道上仅有的两个直线模式区域之一，所以车手们将以约340公里/小时（211英里/小时）的速度到达。这绝对不是你想要出现直线模式故障的地方，就像今年早些时候维斯塔潘的红牛那样。
通过那个墙壁后，你驶入地下通道下方，开始上坡，通过另一个棘手的路段，那里也让许多F3赛车成为受害者。
赛道的突出特征是倾斜的La Monumental弯，但实际上在它之前的弯角在测试中让同样多的F3车手吃亏。
有一个紧凑的减速弯，接着是10号和11号弯的快速右/左连续弯，非常容易出错。
然后你将进入La Monumental，一个24%的倾斜弯，其挑战性使赞德沃特的倾斜弯相形见绌。
倍耐力的首席工程师Simone Berra将其称为锦标赛中“最严酷的弯角”，当The 比赛问他与赞德沃特的倾斜弯相比如何时，Berra说La Monumental对轮胎施加的能量高出20%到30%。
此外，它的出口完全盲区，而且是抓地力限制而非像赞德沃特倾斜弯那样的动力限制，也就是说，为了给车手所需的抓地力，对轮胎和赛车造成了巨大压力。
F3车手在测试中尝试了许多不同的线路，预计F1车手在周五也会这样做。
“感觉就像我在开印地赛车[在椭圆赛道上]，”Slater告诉The 比赛。
“所以是的，这很酷。在F3赛车中它几乎就是全油门。我认为在F2甚至F1中会稍微困难一些。”
“但很难找到正确的线路，因为显然在坡顶处，托底可能会很严重。看起来是一个容易的弯角，但实际上驾驶它，要找到节奏是相当困难的。”
La Monumental只是单圈的一半，之后还有更多具有挑战性的弯角，比如紧凑的17号右弯。
整圈几乎没有喘息的空间，保守驾驶也行不通。
蒙扎F3冲刺赛冠军加藤大翔解释说：“如果你想获得圈速，你必须推进到接近墙壁，所以这很冒险但驾驶起来很有趣。”
F1车手们在蒙扎的车手巡游中交换了对马德里的第一印象，Sainz透露“每个人似乎都对马德里推出的赛道感到相当震惊”。
Sainz，作为本大奖赛的大使，解释说他的意思是震惊于F1增加了一条真正有特色的赛道，而不是近年来加入赛历的一些较为平淡的街道赛道。
detailEn: Formula 1’s new Spanish Grand Prix venue has been described as a “car killer”.
The first-ever race at the brand-new Madring circuit will take place this weekend, but only now are F1 drivers starting to realise what a huge challenge the circuit is going to be.
It’s been described as a mix of Monaco, Macau and Jeddah by those who have already driven it.

It’s an old-school circuit with proper character and corners that have the potential to be instant classics. But there are fears about what kind of race it will produce and how brutal it could be for the cars and drivers.
Having explored the circuit during its construction in June, we’ve since dug more into exactly what kind of challenge the track will present and what we can expect this weekend.
The biggest indicator of that was the two-day Formula 3 test held there a couple of weeks ago.

“In the Formula 3 test there were 19 red flags and three broken chassis, broken suspensions…OK, they’re Formula 3 drivers, but it’s a track that kills cars,” Williams F1 team principal James Vowles told Spanish outlet Sport.
The Race understands some F3 teams were less than impressed by having to test there, because the damaged parts list was very long.

But that F3 test was highly valuable as a pilot episode for F1’s Madrid event, one requested by the circuit organiser to try to avoid the kind of issues that plagued Las Vegas’s debut when errant drain covers disrupted practice, wrecked Carlos Sainz’s Ferrari and infuriated team principal Fred Vasseur.
The chaotic F3 test has also acted as a warning sign for F1 teams and drivers about how much of a challenge it will be.
Ferrari conducted an F1 filming day there back in July, but that was on a much rougher version of the circuit, so the F3 running was the first proper test for the venue.

What’s worrying F1 teams and drivers is that the 19 red flags in F3 were scattered throughout the circuit (see below). It means there isn’t just one danger zone to navigate, as there are so many places where you can come unstuck and find yourself with a hefty repair bill.
With many teams working out their remaining development budget within the 2026 cost cap, the last thing they’ll want is a wrecked car.
We spoke to several F3 drivers and teams to find out why the Madring is so challenging in so many different ways and why there were so many red flags.

Asked why it’s so challenging, Audi-backed F3 championship leader Freddie Slater told The Race: “Because the corners that are there, they're so tight and they're not forgiving and also the walls come at you on the exit of the corners. They don't go away from you like most tracks.
“You're always coming out of the corner and trying to drive away from it instead of maximising, so it's a very tricky track to get in the rhythm of things.
“You have to push otherwise you're slow. So I think that's why it creates so many crashes because if you don't push you're just not on the limit.

“But honestly it's probably one of the best tracks on the calendar in my opinion, just because it's got that old-school feeling to it. Kind of like some of the old-school UK tracks, Macau, places like that. So I'm really excited to have the [F3 championship] finale there.”
The Madring lap starts with a slow-speed chicane akin to Jeddah’s, followed by a flat-out blast through Turns 3 and 4, which builds up into the first real danger zone - the second chicane.
It’s a high-speed chicane where the wall certainly comes at you on the exit, and it was the site of many a crumpled F3 car in the test.
“That's where there's so much laptime because there's uphill section after that, so there's so much laptime to gain going uphill,” Slater said.
“That's why I see a lot of people risking obviously for maximum laptime but also it's probably the place where the most crashes are.
“Also the kerbs are not very forgiving so you have to get it correct otherwise, you're going to end up crashing.”

It’s essentially an even harder version of the now-removed triple-apex Singapore Sling where the trajectory is 'head-first into the wall if you get it slightly wrong'. It’s not anything like some of the laps in the virtual world make it look where you’re able to effortlessly skip over the kerbs.

And the entry to the chicane is one of only two straight mode zones on the circuit, so drivers will be arriving at around 340km/h (211mph). It’s certainly not the kind of place you’d want a straight mode failure like those on Max Verstappen’s Red Bull earlier this year.
Negotiate that wall and you drive beneath the underpass and start climbing uphill through another tricky session that also claimed many an F3 car as a victim.
The standout feature of the circuit is the banked La Monumental corner but actually the corners just before it caught out just as many F3 drivers in the test.
There’s a tight chicane followed by a quick right/left in quick succession at Turns 10 and 11 that’s very easy to get wrong.
That then propels you into La Monumental, a 24% banked corner that dwarfs the challenge of Zandvoort’s banked turns.

Pirelli’s chief engineer Simone Berra labelled it “the most severe turn” in the championship and when The Race asked him how it compared to Zandvoort’s banking, Berra said La Monumental places 20 to 30% higher energy on the tyres.

Plus it has a completely blind exit and it’s grip-limited rather than power-limited like Zandvoort’s banked corner is, i.e. it’s a huge strain on the tyres and cars to give the drivers the grip they need.
F3 drivers were trying lots of different lines during the test and expect F1 drivers to do the same on Friday.
"It feels like I'm in an IndyCar [on an oval]," Slater told The Race.
"So yeah, it's pretty cool. It's just about flat, probably, in a Formula 3 car. I think it's going to be a little bit more difficult in your Formula 2 and maybe even Formula 1.

"But it's quite difficult to get the right line because obviously where the crest is, the bottoming can get quite bad. It looks an easy corner when you look at it but actually to drive it, it's quite a difficult corner to get the rhythm."
La Monumental only marks the halfway point in the lap and there are plenty more challenging corners after that, like the tight Turn 17 right-hander.
There’s very little breathing room around the lap and going conservative doesn’t work either.
Monza F3 sprint race winner Taito Kato explained: “If you want to gain laptime, you have to push until you’re close to the wall, so it’s risky but fun to drive.”
F1 drivers were swapping first impressions of Madrid on the drivers’ parade at Monza, with Sainz revealing “everyone seemed quite shocked by the track that Madrid has come up with”.

Sainz, who is an ambassador for this grand prix, explained he meant shocked in terms of F1 adding a track that has actual character, as opposed to some of the blander street tracks that have joined the calendar in recent years.

items.summaryZh: 法拉利F1青训车手Tuukka Taponen将新落成的马德里赛道赛道形容为“相当耗费体力”且“非常苛刻”，并指出在这条赛道上达到完美非常困难。

items.originalTitle: 法拉利青训车手塔波宁：马德里新赛道“极具挑战”
items.summaryEn: Ferrari F1 junior Tuukka Taponen described the new Madring circuit as "quite physical" and "very demanding", explaining how tough perfection is to reach there. The challenge emerged clearly as successive crashes caused five red flags in one afternoon during an F3 test at the track.
detailZh: “即使是一个小错误也可能让你付出巨大代价”——马德里赛道赛道将如何挑战F1车手
在上个月于F1最新赛道驾驶之后，Tuukka Taponen为本周末的挑战提供了全新的见解
法拉利F1青训车手Tuukka Taponen形容这条全新的马德里赛道赛道“相当耗费体力”且“要求极高”，并解释了在那里要做到完美有多么困难。
Taponen和其他F3车手于8月24日至25日在马德里这条新赛道进行了为期两天的测试，而接二连三的撞车导致一个下午之内出现五次红旗，挑战的规模显而易见。
“这是一条非常难跑的赛道，”这位MP Motorsport车手说。“这里弯道很多——总共有22个——所以要想做出一个干净的单圈并不容易。在长距离和比赛节段中它也相当考验体能，要求很高，因为你需要时刻保持专注。护墙离赛道很近，所以即使是一个小失误也可能让你付出很大代价。”
Taponen指出了那些可能把赛车弹向护墙的棘手路肩，以及在进攻与谨慎之间难以捉摸的平衡，这些都是在这条西班牙赛道上需要掌控的主要因素。
“至少对于参加F3的我们来说，在每个计时段都有可能拉开相当大的差距，”这位芬兰车手补充道。
“我要说第一个计时段可能是最难的，尤其是第二个减速弯。每个人在那里都会压路肩，如果你以稍微错误的角度压上路肩，或者带了一点过多的速度，就可能撞上护墙。你想把车推到极限：如果稍微超出极限，你会冒很大风险，但如果你推得不够，又会损失很多单圈时间。”
“在这个赛段的末尾还有几个高速弯角，到那时轮胎已经开始有点过热了。这让整圈都保持快速和稳定变得相当困难。”
每个人都会在模拟器里做准备，F1车手和年轻车手都一样，但在这个具体情况下，缺乏真实赛道数据是个阻碍。在这里，Taponen 的赛道实测让他注意到赛道的抓地力并不一致。
“一旦你到了那里，现实可能与（模拟器）截然不同，”他解释道。“每个弯角的抓地力水平都不一样：有些感觉抓地力稍差，有些则稍好。这将是 Charles [Leclerc] 和 Lewis [Hamilton] 面临的重大挑战之一。他们还将以非常高的速度行驶，护墙很近，容错空间非常小。在仍然逼近极限的同时跑出一圈干净的圈速将会很困难。”
Taponen 将以无争冠机会的状态迎接 F3 赛季收官战，他将在这一级别的第二个赛季结束。这位法拉利青训车手上一站蒙扎拿到了本赛季首个领奖台，而且令人难以置信的是，他距离排名第三的 Ernesto Rivera 仅差 12 分——尽管排名低了六位。与此同时，表现稳定的前列车手 Freddie Slater 和 Ugo Ugochukwu 将为总冠军展开争夺。
detailEn: “Even a small mistake can cost you a lot” – How Madring will challenge F1 drivers
After driving on F1’s newest track last month, Tuukka Taponen provides fresh insight into this weekend’s challenge
Ferrari Formula 1 junior Tuukka Taponen has described the new Madring circuit as “quite physical” and “very demanding”, explaining how tough perfection is to reach there.

Taponen and other Formula 3 drivers were out on track for a two-day test at Madrid’s new circuit on 24-25 August, and the scale of the challenge noticeably emerged as successive crashes caused five red flags in one single afternoon.

“It’s a very difficult track,” the MP Motorsport driver said. “There are a lot of corners – 22 in total – so it’s not easy to put together a clean lap. It’s also quite physical over long runs and race stints, and very demanding because you need to stay focused all the time. The walls are quite close, so even a small mistake can cost you a lot.”
Taponen pointed to tricky kerbs that can propel cars into barriers, and an elusive compromise between pushing and prudence, as some of the main factors to master at the Spanish circuit.
“At least for us in Formula 3, it was possible to make quite a big difference in every sector,” the Finn added.

“I would say the first sector is probably the most difficult, especially the second chicane. Everyone rides the kerbs there, and if you take one at a slightly wrong angle or carry a little too much speed, you can end up in the wall. You want to push right to the limit: if you go slightly over it, you risk quite a lot, but if you don’t push enough, you can lose a lot of lap time.

“Towards the end of the sector there are also a few high-speed corners, by which point the tyres are already starting to overheat a little. That makes it quite difficult to be quick and consistent throughout the lap.”

Everyone will have prepared in the simulator, F1 drivers and junior racers alike, but the lack of real-world data is a hindrance in this specific case. Here, Taponen’s track action allowed him to notice the track’s grip was inconsistent.

“Once you get there, the reality can be quite different [from the sim],” he explained. “The grip level isn’t the same in every corner: some feel a little less grippy, others a little more. That is going to be one of the big challenges for Charles [Leclerc] and Lewis [Hamilton]. They will also be travelling at very high speeds, with the walls close and very small margins for error. Putting together a clean lap while still pushing to the limit is going to be difficult.”

Taponen is going into F3’s season finale with no title chance as he concludes his second campaign at this level. The Ferrari protege claimed his first podium finish of the season last time out in Monza and, incredibly, lies just 12 points adrift of third-placed Ernesto Rivera – but six spots lower. Meanwhile, consistent frontrunners Freddie Slater and Ugo Ugochukwu will battle it out for the crown.

“为了这项运动，也为了法拉利，我希望，就像刘易斯（Lewis）那样，也许在10年、15年之后，当 Kimi 取得了许多成就时，他可能会成为一名法拉利车手。有朝一日能拥有他，对法拉利来说将是件很棒的事。”他说。

基米·安东内利（安东内利）回顾了他从第19位发车到夺冠的蒙扎惊艳胜利，追上队友乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔），夺得一座具有里程碑意义的主场冠军，并扩大了他的积分榜领先优势

detailEn: Kimi Antonelli driving for Mercedes rather than Ferrari has taken pressure off Italian says Karun Chandhok

On the latest episode of Sky Sports F1's The F1 Show, Simon Lazenby, Karun Chandhok and David Croft discuss Kimi Antonelli's stunning win at Monza; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1

Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok believes Kimi Antonelli driving for Mercedes, rather than Ferrari, has taken some pressure off the Italian.

Antonelli joined the Mercedes junior programme as an 11-year-old after some remarkable results in karting and quickly rose up the motorsport ranks to Formula 1 and replaced Lewis Hamilton at the Silver Arrows only last year.

He currently leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from team-mate George Russell ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid and is on course to become the youngest world champion in F1 history at 20 years old.

His father, Marco Antonelli, has previously revealed he held discussions with Ferrari but the Scuderia did not want to sign someone so young whereas Mercedes were willing to take the risk.

On the latest episode of The F1 Show, Chandhok said: "I actually think by not making him a Ferrari junior, not putting him in front of Ferrari, not trying to make him a Ferrari young driver, and going down the Mercedes path, is actually the best thing that Marco Antonelli has done for his son. It's taken the pressure off in so many ways.
"Could you imagine if he was there as a Ferrari Italian driver? The pressure would be unbelievable. And Mercedes have done a fantastic job of nurturing him and bringing him here.

"I saw Kimi's parents and his sister afterwards by the Mercedes motorhome. They looked so delighted with the fact that obviously he'd won the home Grand Prix. I couldn't help but think they've managed to take away some pressure by not having him as a Ferrari driver."
Kimi Antonelli wins the Italian Grand Prix from 19th on the grid
Last week, Antonelli played down suggestions that he could drive for Ferrari in the future as he claimed he could spend his entire career with Mercedes.
He said "as much as Ferrari is massive, incredible brand, I am very happy where I am" but Chandhok hopes he does drive in red one day.

"For the sake of the sport and the sake of Ferrari, I hope, a bit like Lewis, in 10, 15 years' time when Kimi's achieved a whole lot of things, maybe he will become a Ferrari driver. It'll be great for Ferrari to have him one day," he said.

Antonelli has stunned most of the F1 paddock this year with his speed and performances so far, but his most recent in Monza where he won from 19th on the grid made headlines around the world.
Sky Sports F1's David Croft says Antonelli is a "generational talent" but is still "keeping his feet on the ground".

"At the start of the weekend he was getting pranked in the paddock, getting cream pies flung at him from his team as they got him back with a birthday surprise. I'm not sure the majority of F1 drivers on the grid would have stood for that," said Croft.

"Kimi absolutely revelled in it and there is a driver who is so at ease and so comfortable in the team that he's in. Long may that continue on track and off it as well. He is a total breath of fresh air for Formula 1."

Chandhok added: "He's been prepared from a much younger age as a professional, all-rounded driver - how to work with a team, how to work with a bigger structure.
"These kids now who are being signed to driver programmes from the ages of 10, 11, 12 in junior karting, they're being moulded from a younger age.
"You compare and contrast to the generation above, a Fernando Alonso or a Michael Schumacher, they only signed to professional contracts by the time they were already in F3.

"So I think, in some ways, it's not a surprise, I guess, that he is arriving as a more finished package because he's had 10 years of being as part of a professional structure, which the generation above wasn't."

现年11岁的卡丁车手罗宾·莱科宁（Robin Raikkonen）——出生于基米·莱科宁2015年重返法拉利的第二个赛季之前——在蒙扎比赛周末期间曾传出将加入红牛的消息。

虽然距离能够参加方程式比赛还有好几年，莱科宁已经在卡丁车领域取得了不俗的成绩，在国内和国际赛事中都曾夺冠。
“Robin 已经在卡丁车运动中展现出了非凡的能力，”红牛车队领队 Laurent Mekies 说道。
“他的速度、比赛技巧和天赋已经确立了他作为同龄组中最有前途的年轻车手之一的地位。与此同时，他的成熟、沉稳的态度以及对驾驶的专注也令人印象深刻。"
“我们的目标是一步一步地培养他，不给他肩上施加任何不必要的压力。"
“赛车运动的道路是漫长的，我们会给予他所需的时间、支持和资源，以最大限度地发挥他的潜力。"
我们坚信，只要得到合适的人、合适的文化和合适的环境支持，人才就能茁壮成长。这正是我们致力于为Robin提供的，因为他将继续自己的发展。
我们非常期待与Robin及其家人一起，在他的征程中迈出下一步。
Robin的父亲Kimi补充道："Robin被选中加入红牛青训车队以继续他的赛车之路，我们都为此感到无比激动和兴奋。
"在我们所有的讨论过程中，Laurent以及红牛的其他所有人都给予了我们极大的支持。他们提供了一个极具吸引力且全面的培养计划，将在未来数年中发展和培育Robin的进步，并为他提供发展其天赋所需的一切经验——这种天赋在他迄今为止的所有卡丁车赛事中都已充分展现。"
Kimi表示，Robin将带着“极大的谦逊”加入该计划，并且他的儿子会“全力以赴，以回报红牛对他的信任”。
F1冠军Raikkonen从未效力过红牛车队，但他曾在法拉利与红牛最著名的青训产品之一Sebastian Vettel做过队友，而且他与另一位红牛车手（维斯塔潘）也有过大量的比赛交手经验。
他还在2001年效力于索伯车队时完成了自己的F1首秀，当时该车队以红牛索伯 Petronas车队的名义参赛，不过这并非没有争议；让当时21岁的Raikkonen出场的决定令红牛颇为不满，因为红牛原本希望由Enrique Bernoldi进入该车队。
当Robin明年加入时，红牛青训计划将由Gwen Lagrue负责领导。
拉格鲁格（Lagrue）曾主导梅赛德斯的青训工作，包括将基米·安东内利（安东内利）在青训梯队中培养成才，他实际上是在接替赫尔穆特·马尔科（Helmut Marko），成为该项目的负责人。
detailEn: The son of the 2007 Formula 1 world champion Kimi Raikkonen will join Red Bull's driver development programme next year.
The 11-year-old karter Robin Raikkonen - born just before Kimi Raikkonen's second season back with Ferrari in 2015 - had been rumoured to join Red Bull over the Monza weekend.
Red Bull has now announced it will add Robin to its junior team from 2027.
While years away from being able to race in single-seaters, Raikkonen has already enjoyed strong success in karting, winning at both a national and international level.
"Robin has already demonstrated exceptional ability in karting," Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said.

"His speed, racecraft and natural talent have established him as one of the most promising young drivers in his age group. At the same time, he impresses with his maturity, his calm approach and his clear focus on driving.
"Our goal is to develop him step-by-step, without placing any unnecessary pressure on his shoulders.
"The path through motorsport is a long one, and we will give him the time, support and resources he needs to maximise his potential.

"We strongly believe that talent can thrive when supported by the right people, the right culture and the right environment. That is what we are committed to providing Robin as he continues his development.
"We are very much looking forward to taking the next steps in his journey together with Robin and his family."
Robin’s father Kimi added: "We are all thrilled and excited that Robin has been chosen to further his racing path as a member of the Red Bull junior team.

"Laurent and everyone else at Red Bull have been incredibly supportive throughout all our discussions. They offer a compelling and comprehensive programme to develop and nurture Robin's progress over the coming years and provide him with all the experience required to develop his natural talent, which has amply been displayed in all his karting endeavours to date."
Kimi said Robin joins the programme with "great humility" and that his son would "dedicate all his efforts to warrant the trust that Red Bull is placing in him".

F1 champion Raikkonen never raced for Red Bull but he was team-mates with one of its most famous products, Sebastian Vettel, at Ferrari, and he had plenty of experience racing the other (Max Verstappen).

He also made his F1 debut in 2001 with Sauber, when it ran as the Red Bull Sauber Petronas team, though this was not without controversy; The decision to field the then-21-year-old Raikkonen disgruntled Red Bull, which wanted Enrique Bernoldi placed at the team instead.
The Red Bull junior programme will be led by Gwen Lagrue when Robin joins next year.
Lagrue, who had spearheaded Mercedes' junior efforts including developing Kimi Antonelli through the junior ladder, is effectively replacing Helmut Marko as the head of the programme.

detailZh: 红牛签约基米·莱科宁之子担任青训车手
十一岁的Robin Raikkonen将加入红牛青训队
Minttu Raikkonen、Robin Raikkonen、Kimi Raikkonen、Laurent Mekies、红牛车队
2007年F1世界冠军Kimi之子Robin Raikkonen已被红牛青训队签下。
Raikkonen 出生于2015年1月27日，自2022年以来一直活跃于卡丁车运动，参加过 Rotax Max Challenge 赛事，先是在瑞士，随后遍及整个欧洲。他去年还参加了 WSK Super Master Series。在上述两种情况下，他参加的都是符合其年龄组别的比赛。
“Robin 被选中加入 红牛 青训 红牛青训车队以继续他的赛车之路，我们全家都感到无比激动和兴奋，”新闻稿中援引 Kimi Raikkonen 的话说。
“Laurent 以及 红牛 的其他所有人，在我们整个洽谈过程中都给予了极大的支持。他们提供了一个极具吸引力且完善的项目，在未来几年里培养和促进 Robin 的成长，并为他提供发展其天赋所需的一切经验——他的天赋在迄今为止的所有卡丁车赛事中都得到了充分的展现。
“红牛 的青训车队多年来取得了令人难以置信的成功。其培养过的车手包括 Sebastian Vettel 和 维斯塔潘 等众多名将。因此，Robin 怀着无比谦逊的心情加入这个享有盛誉的项目，他将全力以赴，以不负 红牛 对他的信任。”
红牛F1车队领队Laurent Mekies形容Robin Raikkonen是他这一代“最有前途的年轻车手之一”，称其“已经在卡丁车领域展现出了非凡的能力”。
Mekies热情洋溢地称赞这位年轻的芬兰车手的“速度、比赛技巧和天赋”，以及“他的成熟、冷静的态度和对驾驶的专注”。
这位法国人补充道：“我们的目标是循序渐进地培养他，不给他肩上施加任何不必要的压力。赛车运动的道路很漫长，我们会给他所需的时间、支持和资源，以最大限度地发挥他的潜力。”
“我们坚信，在合适的人、合适的文化和合适的环境的支持下，天赋才能茁壮成长。这正是我们致力于为Robin提供的，让他继续自己的成长。我们非常期待与Robin和他的家人一起，在他的旅程中迈出下一步。”
Robin Raikkonen加入了红牛青训车队的另外九名车手之列，该车队由F2锦标赛领跑者Nikola Tsolov领衔，据信他是争夺2027赛季小红牛席位的热门人选。
Raikkonen的签约正值前梅赛德斯人才观察员Gwen Lagrue准备在红牛担任类似职位之际。
detailEn: Red Bull signs Kimi Raikkonen’s son as junior driver
Eleven-year-old Robin Raikkonen is joining the Red Bull Junior Team
Minttu Raikkonen, Robin Raikkonen, Kimi Raikkonen, Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing
Robin Raikkonen, the son of 2007 Formula 1 world champion Kimi, has been signed to the Red Bull Junior Team.

Raikkonen was born on 27 January 2015 and has been active in karting since 2022, having competed in the Rotax Max Challenge, first in Switzerland, then across Europe. He also took part in the WSK Super Master Series last year. In both cases, that was in age-appropriate categories.
“We are all thrilled and excited that Robin has been chosen to further his racing path as a member of the Red Bull Junior Team,” Kimi Raikkonen was quoted as saying in the press release.

“Laurent and everyone else at Red Bull have been incredibly supportive throughout all our discussions. They offer a compelling and comprehensive programme to develop and nurture Robin’s progress over the coming years and provide him with all the experience required to develop his natural talent, which has amply been displayed in all his karting endeavours to date.

“Red Bull’s Junior Team has had years of incredible success. Its alumni include Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen amongst many others. It is thus with great humility that Robin joins this illustrious programme, and he will dedicate all his efforts to warrant the trust that Red Bull is placing in him.”
Red Bull F1 team principal Laurent Mekies described Robin Raikkonen as “one of the most promising young drivers” of his generation, having “already demonstrated exceptional ability in karting”.
Mekies rhapsodically praised the young Finn for “his speed, racecraft and natural talent” as well as “his maturity, his calm approach and his clear focus on driving”.

“Our goal is to develop him step by step, without placing any unnecessary pressure on his shoulders,” the Frenchman added. “The path through motorsport is a long one, and we will give him the time, support and resources he needs to maximise his potential.

"We strongly believe that talent can thrive when supported by the right people, the right culture and the right environment. That is what we are committed to providing Robin as he continues his development. We are very much looking forward to taking the next steps in his journey together with Robin and his family.”

Robin Raikkonen joins nine other drivers in the Red Bull Junior Team, which is spearheaded by Formula 2 championship leader Nikola Tsolov, who is believed to be a favourite for a Racing Bulls drive in the 2027 F1 season.
Raikkonen's signing occurs as former Mercedes talent scout Gwen Lagrue prepares to take on a similar role at Red Bull.

items.summaryZh: 勒克莱尔在意大利大奖赛蒙扎站以超过230公里/小时的速度失控撞车退赛，但由于引擎未受严重损坏，他不会在本周末的西班牙大奖赛受到发车位罚退。

items.originalTitle: 勒克莱尔蒙扎高速撞车未损引擎，西班牙大奖赛免于罚退
items.summaryEn: Charles Leclerc crashed out of the Italian Grand Prix at Monza after losing control at more than 230km/h, but his engine avoided serious damage so he will not face a grid penalty at this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix.
detailZh: 夏尔·勒克莱尔将不会因蒙扎撞车而在F1西班牙大奖赛受到引擎处罚
这位法拉利车手上周末在意大利大奖赛遭遇严重撞车，但引擎并未受到严重损坏
夏尔·勒克莱尔在蒙扎的高速撞车中成功避免了引擎损坏，因此本周末的F1西班牙大奖赛将不会受到发车位处罚。
这位法拉利车手在周日意大利大奖赛的第二圈退赛，此前他在超过230公里/小时的速度下于帕拉波利卡弯（Parabolic）失控。
这一情况起因是赛车在驶过一处排水沟时发生弹跳，导致正在防守迈凯伦车手奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里的勒克莱尔冲出赛道，撞上了轮胎墙。
不过这台SF-26经受住了超过50G减速的冲击，本周末在马德里只需更换变速箱壳体，而不必换上整套全新的动力单元。
西班牙大奖赛是法拉利再次尝试ADUO引擎升级包的机会，该升级在蒙扎首次亮相，不过车队确认它并非“改变格局”的利器。
总的来说，蒙扎对这支意大利车队来说令人失望，他们仅通过刘易斯·汉密尔顿的第六名拿到八个积分，而且两位车手在第一圈还险些相撞。
这使得法拉利落后于车手积分榜领跑者梅赛德斯122分，梅赛德斯在蒙扎再次获胜，冠军由安东内利夺得，这意味着他成为自1966年卢多维科·斯卡菲奥蒂以来首位赢得意大利本土大奖赛的意大利车手。
detailEn: Charles Leclerc to avoid F1 Spanish GP engine penalty despite Monza crash
The Ferrari driver suffered a big crash at last weekend's Italian GP, but the engine was not severely damaged
Charles Leclerc managed to avoid engine damage in his high-speed crash at Monza so will not receive a grid penalty for this weekend’s Formula 1 Spanish Grand Prix.
The Ferrari driver retired on lap two of the Italian Grand Prix on Sunday after losing control of his car through the Parabolic at more than 230km/h.
It came as the result of a bounce over a water drain causing Leclerc, who was defending from the McLaren of Oscar Pisatri, to run wide and into the tyre barrier.
But the SF-26 withstood the impact, with deceleration exceeding 50G, and will only have the transmission casing replaced and not an entirely new power unit for Madrid this weekend.
The Spanish Grand Prix marks another chance for Ferrari to try its ADUO engine upgrade, which it debuted at Monza, though the team confirmed it isn’t a ‘game changer’.
Monza on the whole was disappointing for the Italian outfit which only scored eight points via Lewis Hamilton’s sixth-placed result while both drivers almost collided on the opening lap.

That leaves Ferrari 122 points behind championship leader Mercedes, who won again at Monza via Kimi Antonelli meaning he became the first Italian to win his home race since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

items.titleZh: F1马德里新赛事首秀：马德里赛道赛道前瞻
items.summaryZh: 本周末F1将在马德里的马德里赛道赛道迎来45年来首次马德里站的比赛，该赛事获得了为期10年的西班牙大奖赛举办权。这条57圈的赛道被称为“双头怪兽”般的布局，车手和车队需要时间从工程角度加以理解。

media.altZh: F1马德里新赛事首秀：马德里赛道赛道前瞻

items.originalTitle: F1马德里新赛事首秀：Madring赛道前瞻
items.summaryEn: Formula 1 will race in Madrid for the first time in 45 years this weekend at the Madring circuit, which has secured a 10-year tenure of the Spanish Grand Prix. The 57-lap circuit is described as a two-headed monster that will take drivers and teams some time to understand from an engineering perspective.
detailZh: 随着马德里赛道赛道首秀，F1最新一站比赛值得期待什么
时隔45年，一级方程式本周末将首次在马德里比赛，赛道是具有双重特性的马德里赛道
马德里将承办西班牙大奖赛为期十年，从如今改为两年一届的巴塞罗那比赛中接过了这一名号，这是F1将赛事带到城市人口中心的最新举措。
比赛将在一条拥有“双头怪兽”之称的赛道上进行57圈，车手和车队需要一些时间才能让他们的工程思维完全理解这条赛道。
所谓的马德里赛道赛道最初的效果图引发了褒贬不一的反应，人们担心西班牙大奖赛从巴塞罗那的永久性赛道迁至马德里主机场附近的Valdebebas地区后，F1会再添一条千篇一律的街道赛，一个很快就会被弃用的钢筋水泥丛林。甚至无需走出西班牙国界，就能让人想起早已停办的瓦伦西亚大奖赛——那场在如今已成幽灵赛道上举办的、如海鲜饭锅般昙花一现的乏味比赛。
我们六月对现场的首次考察表明，这条最初由Dromo设计、后期施工阶段移交给Tilke完成的赛道，其最终成品Certainly远没有那些传言那么糟糕。但它也确实与赛历上其他任何一条赛道都不相同。
起终点直道周围区域位于IFEMA会展中心的广场和公共道路上，这无疑让第一个赛段有一种走走停停的感觉，令人联想到迈阿密和新加坡之类的赛道。
最醒目的地标，也是比赛官方海报和其他宣传材料上的主角，是La Monumental；这是一条长而快的倾斜弯道，坡度达到了允许的最大值24%。这条550米长的弯道比赞德沃特那条大致可类比的最后弯要长得多，因为它环绕赛道北端专门修建的区域划出了一个270度的弧线。
纪念碑赛道的陡峭弯道倾角具有不断变化的坡度和高度
这座高耸的弯道外侧设有大看台，其坡度、半径和高度的持续变化使其与赛历上的其他倾斜弯道或椭圆形赛道上的弯道截然不同，亲临现场时给人留下了震撼的印象。这里没有缓冲区，但外侧装有SAFER护栏。
“这是一个非常非常特别的弯道，” 勒克莱尔 在与法拉利进行尘土飞扬的拍摄日并勘察该弯道后说道。“在这个弯道，我感觉在排位赛中我们必须非常勇敢，因为它将达到极限。
“我确实相信它有潜力成为本赛季最具标志性的弯道之一，尤其是配上那个大看台。这将为这个弯道的体验增色。有一点是肯定的，那就是你必须全身心地投入。”
那个弯角之后是一连串的高速变向，而且缓冲区很小。正如一次红旗频出的F3测试所表明的那样，这条赛道在第一年将很难应付。
初步迹象表明，马德里赛道 即使不会成为车手们最喜欢的赛道，也将是在排位赛中颇具挑战性的赛道。不过，这条赛道能否呈现精彩的比赛场面，目前还没有定论。由于拥有众多制动区，这条赛道在能量回收的难度方面应该处于中游水平。超车看起来并不容易，3号弯和5号弯之间的直道是最明显的超车机会。
"这将是一条非常有挑战性的赛道，"Leclerc 委婉地说。"我不知道超车情况如何，我不确定会有很多超车，我希望我错了。但我认为排位赛以及驾驶这样一条赛道的挑战，将会是本赛季最酷的体验之一。"
马德里能为F1提供什么，而巴塞罗那仍在为此苦苦挣扎
马德里真正想做出差异化的是它的交通可达性。这条赛道不仅距离机场很近，还与马德里庞大的地铁和市郊铁路网络相连。主办方承诺从首都任何地方都能便捷无阻地抵达赛道，而这长期以来正是巴塞罗那的一大痛点。
在这方面，它正是F1管理层如今所青睐的那类场馆。一场与“目的地城市”深度融合的城市比赛，拥有各种配套设施、内置的交通与可持续解决方案，以及容纳大规模VIP设施的空间。
“嗯，你比我更清楚，进出一条传统赛道有多麻烦。这里南边有地铁，北边有市郊铁路，将会非常方便，”IFEMA的首席运营官Carlos Jimenez承诺道，“这两条线路都很快、停靠站很少，因为它们的设计初衷就是快速连接机场和市中心。所以，我们认为车迷抵达赛道的体验将是一个决定性的优势。
“这非常便利，但代价是我们必须更加努力，才能提供良好的现场体验。否则，车迷们会很快回到市里的酒店和餐厅，因为我们是在和市中心竞争。”
三级方程式（Formula 3）于八月底在该赛道进行了测试。
马德里能否兑现其承诺，顺利举办一届最多可容纳11万名观众的首届赛事，仍有待观察。最近有许多首届比赛成为学习机会的例子，包括迈阿密和拉斯维加斯。F1重返马德里很可能也会有不完善之处，但组织者表示他们已为此做好准备。
“这并不容易，”费尔南多·阿隆索（阿隆索）的前经纪人、现任该赛事总经理的路易斯·加西亚·阿巴德（Luis Garcia Abad）说，“我参与F1已经有25年了，我从没想过就你需要顾及的所有事情而言，会这么困难。”
“我一直与所有推广人交流，当你试图从零开始打造某样东西时，问题或多或少都是一样的。但IFEMA给我们提供了很多解决方案。我们本来没有赛道，但我们有Wi-Fi，有电力，主入口处还有地铁站。如果你试图在一个不同的场地组织赛事，那简直是一场噩梦。但有了这些（已经具备的）条件，我们得以把它建起来。”
“现在我们必须尽力提供我们能提供的最佳客户体验。”
detailEn: What to expect from F1's newest race as Madring debuts
For the first time in 45 years, Formula 1 will race in Madrid this weekend at the dual-natured Madring circuit
Madrid's 10-year tenure of the Spanish Grand Prix, taking over the moniker from the now biennial Barcelona race, is Formula 1's latest effort to bring its series to urban population centres.
It does so for 57 laps on a two-headed monster of a circuit that will take drivers and teams some time to wrap their collective engineering minds around.

Initial concept renderings of the so-called Madring drew mixed reactions with fears the Spanish GP's move from Barcelona's permanent circuit to the Valdebebas area near Madrid's main airport would see F1 add another generic street circuit, a concrete jungle that would soon be abandoned. One doesn't even have to look beyond the Spanish borders to evoke memories of the long-defunct Valencia grand prix, an uninspired flash in a paella-sized pan on what is now a ghost track.

Our first site visit in June suggested the circuit – originally designed by Dromo before the final stages of construction were handed over to Tilke – showed that the end product is certainly nowhere near as dramatic as that. But it certainly isn't like any other circuit on the calendar either.

The area around the start-and-finish straight is located around the IFEMA fairground concourse and public access roads, which certainly gives the first sector a stop-start feel reminiscent of the likes of Miami and Singapore.

The standout landmark, which features on the race official poster and other promotional material, is La Monumental; a long, fast banked corner featuring the maximum allowed 24% inclination. The 550-metre corner is much longer than Zandvoort's somewhat comparable final turn, as it draws a 270-degree arc around the northern, purpose-built end of the circuit.
The steep banking of La Monumental has a continuously changing gradient and elevation

The towering corner, which features a grandstand on the outside, made a staggering impression in person because of its continuous changes in gradient, radius and elevation that sets it apart from other banked corners on the calendar, or those found in oval races. There is no runoff, but the outside is lined with a SAFER barrier.

"It's a very, very special corner," Charles Leclerc said after exploring it during a dusty filming day with Ferrari. "It's a corner where I feel in qualifying we'll have to be very brave because it's going to be on the limit.

"I do believe it can become one of the most iconic corners of the season, especially with the grandstand. That will add to the experience of that corner. One thing is for sure, and that's that you will have to have full commitment."
That corner is followed by a number of high-speed direction changes with little run-off. As a red-flag-ridden F3 test suggested, the circuit will be tricky to handle in year one.

Early indications suggest that the Madring, if not an outright driver favourite, will be a respectable driving challenge in qualifying. The jury is still out on whether the circuit will be able to deliver a compelling spectacle, though. Because of its many braking zones, the circuit should sit in the middle of the pack in terms of energy-harvesting challenges. Overtaking does not look particularly easy, with the straight between Turns 3 and 5 the most obvious opportunity.

"It's going to be a very challenging track," Leclerc said diplomatically. "I don't know about the overtakes, I'm not sure there will be that many overtakes, I hope I'm wrong. But I think qualifying and the challenge of driving such a track is going to be one of the very cool ones of the season."
What Madrid can offer F1 that Barcelona still struggles with

Where Madrid wants to make a real difference is its accessibility. The circuit is not just a close drive from the airport, but is also connected to Madrid's extensive underground and commuter train network. The organisers promise hassle-free access to the circuit from anywhere in the capital, something which has long been a pain point in Barcelona.

In that respect it is exactly the type of venue that F1 management has become infatuated with. An urban race well integrated into a 'destination city', with all the amenities, baked-in mobility and sustainability solutions, and room for extensive VIP facilities.

"Well, you know better than me that coming in and out of a traditional circuit is a nightmare. Here we have both the metro in the south and the commuter train in the north, which is going to be extremely convenient," IFEMA's COO Carlos Jimenez promised. "Both are very fast lines with very few stops because they were designed to quickly connect the airport with the city centre. So, the experience for the fans to reach the circuit, we think it's going to be a difference-maker.

"It's very convenient, but the counterpart is that it obliges us to work harder to provide a good experience. Otherwise, the fans will quickly go back to the hotels and restaurants in the city, because we are competing with the city centre."
Formula 3 conducted a track test at the circuit at the end of August

Whether or not Madrid can make good on its promise to organise a smooth inaugural edition of its event, for a maximum capacity of 110,000 spectators, remains to be seen. There have been many recent examples of year one being a learning opportunity, including Miami and Las Vegas. F1's return to Madrid will likely be rough around the edges, too, but the organisers say they are prepared for that.

"It's not easy," said Luis Garcia Abad, Fernando Alonso's former manager and now the managing director of the event. "I have been involved in F1 for the last 25 years and I never thought that it was going to be so difficult in terms of all the things that you have to be aware of.

"I have been speaking with all the promoters, and the problems are more or less the same when you are trying to build something from scratch. But IFEMA gave us a lot of solutions. We didn't have a racetrack, but we had Wi-Fi, we had energy, we had a metro station at the main entrance. If you are trying to organise something in a different circuit, it's a nightmare. But with all these parameters [already in place], we were able to build it.
"Now we have to deliver the best customer experience we can."

这条全长3.365英里的马德里赛道（马德里赛道）共有22个官方弯道，不过不寻常的是赛道布局中包含了5A号弯和20A号弯——所以也许实际上有24个弯道。
无论具体号码是多少，在起终点直道之后，车手几乎总会在某个时刻转动方向盘，因为这条赛道几乎没有直道。
1号和2号组成的左右减速弯是整条赛道上为数不多的超车点之一，因为这里有一段很重的刹车区，随后经过3号和4号弯的长距离全油门路段，驶向可以说是自2008年至2012年新加坡大奖赛使用的老“新加坡甩尾”减速弯（Singapore Sling）以来一级方程式中最别扭的一个减速弯。
车手在5号弯能用到多少速度、能压上多少路肩，将是这条赛道的关键点之一。如果赛车并排进入5号弯前的路段，请屏住呼吸，因为那里根本容不下两辆赛车并排通过。然而，减速弯之前那段长长的全油门区域意味着车手会渴望在这里尝试超车……
在那之后，赛道上下起伏，进入7号弯一个非常棘手的上坡刹车区，在那里我们可能会看到车手擦碰到外侧的护栏。
赛道随后向左、向右、再向左转弯，到了排位赛时，由于练习赛中已经留下大量橡胶使赛道干净，这段或许可以全油门通过。
接下来是12号弯，它有可能成为标志性弯角，名为“拉蒙纽门塔尔（La Monumental）”。这是一个巨大的倾角弯道，以百分之二十四的坡度（13.5度）完成180度转弯，车手将在承受巨大横向G力的同时，尽量长时间保持全油门。
在13号弯向左轻摆之后，接下来的几个弯应该都可以全油门通过，直到来到17号弯这个90度的右弯，随后车手高速穿越18号和19号弯，再重刹进入20号弯这个急促的左弯。
最后一个弯即22号弯，是一个90度右弯，内侧护栏向外突出，因此车手在驶上主直道完成一圈过山车般的单圈时，需要小心不要过多切弯心，排位赛中这一圈预计用时约90秒。
法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔，加上威廉姆斯的卡洛斯·塞恩斯，是仅有的几位有过在这条赛道驾驶经验的车手。
塞恩斯是马德里环形赛道（马德里赛道）的形象大使，并对12号弯“La Monumental”倾斜弯道提出了意见，以便赛道设计者能够确保其安全性，同时保留独特性。
勒克莱尔说：“这是一个非常、非常特别的弯角。在这个弯角，我感觉在排位赛中，我们得——我用礼貌的方式说——我们必须非常勇敢，因为它将达到极限。
“所以我觉得那会非常酷。它将是一个非常酷的弯角。我相信它可以成为本赛季最具标志性的弯角之一，尤其是等看台建成之后。我认为那也会为这个弯角的体验增添色彩。”
甲骨文红牛车队将沥青路面换成了地下空间，标志性的 小红牛8 赛车驶上了马德里地铁的轨道，进行了一场史无前例的特技表演
勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿在七月进行了一次拍摄日，当时赛道刚刚完工，所以天气极其炎热，尘土飞扬。
汉密尔顿说："正如你所预料的那样，赛道完全没有抓地力。所以你的轮胎基本上全程都覆盖着灰尘。"
"这条赛道看起来会是那种适合排位赛单圈的赛道，而且几乎没有任何直道。所以这里看起来会是一个很难超车的地方。"
首次一睹 F1 最新赛道——马德里赛道 的真容
在赛道的大部分路段，如果车手因为转弯时机不对或车速稍微快了一点而稍稍偏离了赛车线，他们很可能就会高速撞上护栏。
风险与回报的赌注将非常高，而那些最大胆、并且把事情做对的车手将会笑到最后。
塞恩斯说：“我认为，考虑到他们设置护墙的方式以及这条赛道的设计，它肯定会成为最近一级方程式（Formula 1）中最大的挑战之一。”
“这条赛道让我想起很多吉达，让我想起很多巴库，在某些方面甚至还有点像澳门。所以开着有1000马力的一级方程式赛车在这里跑，将会是一个非常有趣的挑战，让我们看看会怎样吧。”
那么我们会遇到安全车和红旗吗？
简而言之，几乎可以肯定会。这条赛道难度极高，问题只是我们在练习赛、排位赛和正赛中会看到多少次红旗。正如我们在意大利大奖赛上看到的那样，如果任何护栏因撞车需要维修，那肯定需要出示红旗。
在为期两天的F3测试中，共出现了19次红旗——尽管并非全部都是因为撞车。
赛恩斯说：“看看这条赛道，再听听F3测试中发生的情况，我想大家都预计在排位赛中会看到安全车、红旗和黄旗，诸如此类的情况。”
“一级方程式最近有一种潮流或趋势，就是去往像吉达、巴库这类更贴近市中心的赛道——还有迈阿密——但那些地方护墙更多，而我们并没有遇到任何问题。实际上我们去过的每一个地方，比赛看起来都进行得相当顺利，所以这正是我们正在延续的类似趋势。”

The Madring street circuit in Madrid is set to be a huge challenge for the drivers as Formula 1 enters the unknown this weekend; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1

Formula 1 has a brand-new track to look forward to this weekend and the expectation is there will be carnage and the drivers will be seriously tested at the Madring.

The Spanish Grand Prix has moved from its traditional circuit in Barcelona to a high-speed street track in Madrid and has been described as "Jeddah on steroids" by Formula 3 drivers who tested there last month - the Jeddah track itself is one of the most challenging circuits in F1.
So why is the Madring so difficult and how will it impact the racing we see this weekend, live on Sky Sports F1?

There are 22 official corners on the 3.365-mile Madring circuit, although unusually the track layout has Turns 5A and 20A - so maybe there are 24.
Whatever the number, after the start/finish straight the driver will almost always be turning the steering wheel at some point as there are few straights.

The left-right chicane of Turns 1 and 2 is one of just a few overtaking spots thanks to its heavy braking zone before a long blast through Turns 3 and 4 towards arguably the most awkward chicane in F1 since the old 'Singapore Sling' chicane which was used at the Singapore Grand Prix between 2008 and 2012.

Just how much speed and how much kerb the drivers can use at Turn 5 will be a critical point of the circuit. If cars go side by side approaching Turn 5, hold your breath, because you cannot fit two cars through there alongside each other. However, the long flat-out zone before the chicane means drivers will be keen to make an overtake here...
After that, the track goes up and down into a really tricky uphill braking zone of Turn 7 where we may see drivers glancing the barriers on the outside.
The track then veers left, right and left, which may be flat out come qualifying when the track is clean after plenty of rubber has gone down from the practice sessions.

Then comes, what could become iconic, Turn 12, known as La Monumental. A huge banked corner that turns 180 degrees at 24 per cent gradient (13.5 degrees) where the drivers will try to stay hard on the throttle as much as possible while experiencing massive G-forces.

After a left-hand flick at Turn 13, the next few corners should be flat out until you arrive at a 90-degree right hander of Turn 17 before the drivers dance through Turns 18 and 19 at high speed, then hit the brakes into a sharp left hander at Turn 20.

The last corner of Turn 22 is a 90-degree right hander where the inside barriers jut out, so the drivers will need to be careful not to cut the apex too much as they arrive on the main straight to complete a rollercoaster lap which should be around 90 seconds in qualifying.
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, plus Williams' Carlos Sainz are the only drivers to have any experience of driving the circuit.
Sainz is a Madring ambassador and gave input on the Turn 12 La Monumental banking so track designers could ensure it is safe, while still being unique.

Leclerc said: "It's a very, very special corner. It's a corner where I feel in qualifying, we'll have to, I will say it in a polite way, but we'll have to be very brave because it's going to be on the limit.

"And so that's going to be really cool, I think. It's going to be a really cool corner. I do believe it can become one of the most iconic corners of the season, especially once the grandstand will be built. I think that will add also to the experience of that corner."
Oracle Red Bull Racing swapped the asphalt for the underground, as the iconic RB8 took to the tracks of the Madrid Metro in a first-of-its-kind stunt
Leclerc and Hamilton conducted a filming day in July when the track had only just finished its completion, so it was extremely hot and dusty.
"As you would expect, there was no grip. So your tyres were basically just covered in dust, and that's the whole time," said Hamilton.
"It looks like it will be a qualifying lap sort of circuit, and there's not really any straights. So it looks like a difficult place to overtake."
A first look at F1's newest circuit - the Madring

For much of the track, if the drivers are slightly off the racing line by turning at the wrong time or carrying a little too much speed, they could easily find themselves in the barriers at high speed.
The risk-versus-reward stakes will be very high and the bravest drivers, who get it right, will come out on top.
"I think definitely with the way they've put the barriers and the design of the track it's going to be one of the biggest challenges in Formula 1 recently," said Sainz.

"The track reminds me a lot of Jeddah, it reminds me a lot of Baku, even reminds me a bit of Macau in some ways. So having that in an F1 [car] with 1,000 horsepower is going to be quite an interesting challenge, so let's see how it goes."
So we are going to get safety cars and red flags?

In short, almost certainly. Such is the difficulty of the track, it is a question of how many red flags will we see across practice, qualifying and the race. As we saw at the Italian Grand Prix, if any barriers need to be repaired for crashes, that will definitely require a red flag.
In the two-day F3 test, there were 19 red flags - albeit not all of them were for crashes.
"Looking at the track and hearing of what happened in the F3 test, I think we are all expecting safety cars, red flags and yellow flags in qualy and things like this," said Sainz.

"It has been a fashion or a tendency of Formula 1 to go to these kind of tracks like Jeddah, Baku recently that are closer to the city - and Miami - but they have more walls and we haven't had any issues with it. The races actually seem to be going quite well to every place we've gone, so it's that similar trend we're going towards."

detailZh: 梅赛德斯正在酝酿一次可能对竞争对手法拉利日渐渺茫的2026年F1冠军希望构成致命打击的引擎升级，该升级借助ADUO机制，即将投入使用。
尽管围场内普遍公认梅赛德斯拥有最完整的动力单元整体方案，但该车队已根据F1的追赶机制——即“额外开发与升级机会”（ADUO）——获得了今年引入一次开发升级的权利。
这是因为国际汽联对各制造商的分析得出结论：以ADUO所依据的内燃机部分来衡量，红牛领先其他所有厂商超过2%。
这意味着梅赛德斯有权在本赛季进行一次动力单元升级，并在2027年再进行一次；而法拉利、奥迪和本田则可以今年进行两次、明年再进行两次。红牛目前则不被允许进行任何改进。
梅赛德斯在本赛季早些时候曾表示，虽然它会利用通过ADUO获得的额外测试台架时间和研发支出，但它并不计划引入任何硬件改动。
然而，The 比赛获悉，计划现在已有改变，梅赛德斯的Brixworth发动机工厂正在进行各项工作，以在本赛季结束前推出一个ADUO升级版本。
升级版发动机的引入时间尚未最终确定，但预计很可能在即将到来的阿塞拜疆、马来西亚和新加坡三连赛期间的某个时点。
这一时机可能与乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔）因启用全新动力单元部件而不得不接受发车退后处罚的时间相吻合，因为他现有的发动机储备无法撑到赛季结束。
梅赛德斯ADUO升级将在哪个区域进行尚未得到确认，但意大利大奖赛上基米·安东内利（安东内利）引入了哪些新部件、没有引入哪些新部件，可能提供了一个重要线索。
这位车手积分榜领跑者在进入他的主场之战前就知道，由于更换发动机的处罚，他将从发车区的最后一位起步。
然而，梅赛德斯没有选择安装一套全新的动力单元，而是将更换限制在安东内利的内燃机、电池和控制电子设备上。
车队没有安装新的涡轮增压器、MGU-K、排气系统和附属部件，尽管更换这些新部件本来不会带来任何额外后果。
推迟引入全套组件，这表明梅赛德斯计划在本赛季晚些时候引入这些部件——到那时，任何这些部件在安装时都还有升级的机会。
人们普遍认为，梅赛德斯通过改进其内燃机（ICE）几乎没有什么收益，而且这样做有可能使其领先于红牛，从而给对手创造使用研发配额的机会。
改进很可能集中在其他领域，其中涡轮增压器是最明显的、可以带来可观收益的部分。
由于梅赛德斯在意大利站采取的策略（即没有更换某些部件），首次引入全新涡轮增压器将不会受到处罚。
因此，当任何ADUO步骤到来时，这可能意味着Russell和Antonelli同时获得它。
根据F1的规则，如果制造商引入一项规格升级，那么该升级必须提供给它旗下的客户车队。
在该升级首次亮相的分站赛上，厂队必须向每支客户车队提供至少一个版本的改动。
因此，当新部件到来时，阿尔派、梅赛德斯和威廉姆斯都将享有所取得的任何进步，即使他们必须选择如何最好地在各自车手之间错开引入时间。
这也可能影响到前沿的争夺战，迈凯伦近期的进步帮助它赢得了比赛，而它可能获得的任何收益都将使其对法拉利拥有进一步的优势。
梅赛德斯ADUO升级的到来，很可能与一次重大赛车升级的时间相近，这次升级预计将在下月初于马来西亚举行的巴林大奖赛上推出。
由于车队今年在研发投入上采取了保守策略，它选择将重大新部件的推出时间间隔拉开。
车队上次推出重大升级套件是在5月底的蒙特利尔，目前正在为雪邦开发可能是一次大规模改革的方案。
汉密尔顿表示梅赛德斯的优势“令人难以置信”
梅赛德斯计划带来一次ADUO升级，这对法拉利来说是个坏消息，后者已在意大利大奖赛上引入了其两次允许升级中的第二次。
据了解，法拉利为提升引擎动力所做的改动与涡轮有关——将设计放大，并对概念进行了其他一些修改，以帮助挖掘其潜力。
法拉利此前淡化了其ADUO 2升级的重要性，哈斯车队的Ollie Bearman也使用了这套升级参赛。
然而，从法拉利与梅赛德斯在蒙扎直道上的相对表现可以清楚地看出，双方之间仍存在很大的差距。
法拉利车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔（Fred Vasseur）表示，车队没有足够的能量来进行真正的对抗，因为对手们采用了不同的能量释放策略。
他说：“[有些车]在一条直道上快10公里/小时，在另一条直道上又慢10公里/小时。问题在于我们几乎在所有地方都慢了10公里/小时。
“当我们在一个弯角多投入一些能量时，接下来一条直道上的差距反而更大。这几乎无法管理。”
刘易斯·汉密尔顿表示，他自己的法拉利与梅赛德斯之间的差距让他感到震惊。
"我们知道他们在直道上很快，但他们在直道上究竟有多快真是令人难以置信，"他说。"梅赛德斯的动力，那玩意儿就是不断地拉、拉、拉。"
尽管瓦塞尔指出了能量部署不足是比赛中的一大限制因素，但他表示，法拉利整体表现不佳并没有明显的根本原因。
"当你缺乏纯粹的动力时，你就得通过调整部署来试图在一条直道上进行补偿，"他说。
“如果你在某处部署得更多，那肯定就会在别处部署得更少。然后在战斗中你就是在陷入一个错误的螺旋，试图去玩弄这个。”
“说实话，这不是关于部署的问题。我认为部署是好的。就连迈凯伦，他们也在周五和周六早上做了一点尝试。归根结底，我们缺少的是纯粹的动力。”
尽管蒙扎的升级是法拉利本赛季进行的第二步改进，此前6月在奥地利引入了修改，但瓦塞尔认为，引擎更改所需的长周期意味着与梅赛德斯抗衡将是一个长期项目。
“我们并没有指望靠ADUO 1或ADUO 2就实现追赶，”他说。“我们正在小步前进，但必须记住的是……哪怕只提升几匹马力，对发车位置来说也是很好的一步。”
detailEn: Mercedes is working on what could be a killer blow to rival Ferrari's fading 2026 Formula 1 title chances with an ADUO-assisted engine upgrade set for introduction.

Despite it being accepted in the paddock that Mercedes has the best complete power unit package, it has earned the right to bring a development step this year under F1's catch-up mechanism known as Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO).

That is because the FIA's analysis of the different manufacturers has concluded that, based on the internal combustion engine element that ADUO is judged on, Red Bull is more than 2% ahead of everybody else.

It means Mercedes has the right to bring one power unit upgrade this season and one in 2027, while Ferrari, Audi and Honda can bring two this year and two next. Red Bull is not allowed any improvements yet.

Mercedes had declared earlier this season that, while it would be making use of the extra test bench hours and development spending that has been opened to it through ADUO, it did not plan to introduce any hardware changes.
However, The Race has learned that there has now been a change of plan and that efforts are ongoing at Mercedes' Brixworth engine facility to ready an ADUO step before the end of the campaign.

No date has yet been set in stone for the introduction of the upgraded specification, but it is anticipated that it will likely be at some point during the upcoming triple header that comprises Azerbaijan, Malaysia and Singapore.

The timing of this could coincide with when George Russell has to take a grid drop penalty for fresh power unit components, with him unable to get through to the end of the season on his current pool.

It has not been confirmed in what area the Mercedes ADUO modifications will be made, but a big clue may have come at the Italian Grand Prix through the new parts Kimi Antonelli did and did not introduce there.
The world championship leader had headed into his home race knowing that he would be starting from the back of the grid because of an engine change penalty.
However, Mercedes chose not to fit a totally new power unit and instead restricted the changes to Antonelli's internal combustion engine, battery and control electronics.
It did not fit a fresh turbo, MGU-K, exhaust and ancillaries, even though taking new versions of these would have been without consequence.
Holding fire on introducing the full suite of components suggests Mercedes plans to bring those parts later this season – with the door then open for any of these to be upgraded when they are fitted.
It is widely understood that Mercedes has little to gain through improving its ICE, and that doing so risks pulling it ahead of Red Bull and handing its rival an opportunity for ADUO.
Modifications are likely to be focused in other areas, with the turbo the most obvious area where good gains can be found.
Due to Mercedes' tactics in Italy, in terms of what it did not replace, bringing the first fresh turbo will be without penalty.
So, when any ADUO step comes then that could mean both Russell and Antonelli getting their hands on it at the same time.
Under F1's rules, if a manufacturer introduces an upgrade of specification, then this has to be made available to its customer teams.
At the first race where it comes, the works squad must make at least one version of the change available to each of its customer teams.
So, when the new part comes, Alpine, Mercedes and Williams will all enjoy any progress that has been made, even if they have to choose how best to stagger any introduction between their drivers.
This could have an impact on the fight at the front too, with McLaren's recent progress having helped it win races and any gain it has potentially giving it a further edge over Ferrari.
The arrival of the Mercedes ADUO upgrade will likely come around the time of a major car upgrade that looks set to arrive at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of next month.
With the team having been conservative with its development spending this year, it has elected to space out its introduction of major new parts.
It last introduced a major package in Montreal in late May, but is working on what could be a big overhaul for Sepang.
Hamilton says Mercedes advantage 'mind blowing'
Mercedes' plan to bring an ADUO upgrade will be bad news for Ferrari, which introduced the second of its two allowed upgrades at the Italian Grand Prix.

It is understood that the changes it made to try to improve engine power were related to the turbo – making the design bigger with some other modification to the concept aimed at helping its potential.
Ferrari had downplayed the significance of its ADUO 2 step, which was also raced by Haas's Ollie Bearman.
However, it was clear from the relative performance of Ferrari against Mercedes on Monza's straights that there remains a big differential in play.
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur said that his team did not have the energy available to fight properly, as rivals battled with different deployment strategies.
"[Some] were 10km/h faster on one straight and 10km/h slower on another," he said. "The issue was that we were almost 10km/h slower everywhere.
"When we were putting a bit more energy in one corner, the gap was even bigger in the next straight line. It was quite impossible to manage."
Lewis Hamilton said he was taken aback by the differences between his own Ferrari and the Mercedes.
"We knew that they were fast on the straight, but it was really mind-blowing just how quick they were on the straight," he said. "Mercedes power, that thing just keeps pulling, pulling, pulling."
Despite Vasseur singling out the deployment deficit as a limiting factor in the race, he said there was no obvious root cause for the overall poor Ferrari performance.
"When you have a lack of pure power, then you start to play with deployment to try to compensate in one straight line," he said.
"If you deploy more somewhere, for sure you will deploy less somewhere else. And then you are going in the wrong spiral to try to play with this when you are fighting.
"Honestly, it's not about deployment. I think deployment was good. Even McLaren, they were playing a little bit Friday and Saturday morning. At the end, we are missing pure power."

Despite the Monza upgrade being the second step that Ferrari has made this season, following the revisions introduced in Austria in June, Vasseur thinks the long lead times for engine changes means getting on terms with Mercedes will be a long-term project.

"We were not expecting to recover [with] ADUO 1 or ADUO 2," he said. "We are doing small steps, but what you have to keep in mind is that…even if you make a couple of horsepower, it's a good step on the grid.
